The reporting date. That is my sticking point, and there is no wiggle room in it: my numbers go to Milan on the fifth, so the Brazilian layer has to be confirmed by the second. On everything else we can split the difference.
The second is tight. Moving my broker deadline is a non-starter, but I would rather find those two days somewhere than argue about them in front of the head.

Nobody teaches you that these small words carry rank. I learned it in my second year reporting into a group function. I wrote to the head of the division and I said, we had better confirm the capacity before Friday. In my head that was helpful. What he heard was an instruction with a threat behind it, from somebody four levels below him, because had better always carries an or else, and the or else is only yours to give if you are the one who can act on it. Between peers it is fine. Downwards it is fine. Upwards it lands like a warning, and nobody will ever tell you that it did. The safe version costs you three words. I would rather we confirmed the capacity before Friday. Same request, same urgency, no threat. And if the answer comes back no, would rather still leaves you somewhere to stand. Had better does not.

I stopped walking into those conversations with a recommendation. I go in with three options and what each one costs, on one page, and I have never regretted it. The reason is not tidiness. A recommendation invites the other person to argue with me. An options sheet invites them to argue with the options, which is a much shorter argument and a far less personal one. Two things I have learned to put on the page. Say which one you would go for and say why, because a sheet with no view on it looks like you could not make up your mind. And name your sticking point out loud, the one thing you cannot move on, before anybody asks you for it. Everything else you can split the difference on. Leave it unsaid and the other side spends the whole meeting testing where the wall is, and you spend it defending a line you never drew.

We have weighed up the three options, and on balance the second is the lesser evil. I would rather hold off until the January renewals than commit capacity we may need in the south. The one sticking point is the reporting date, and on that there is no wiggle room. On everything else we may as well split the difference and take one sheet to Milan.
